tagline: Sera — the autonomous auto-research harness for inference
customer_result: An extractive question-answering pipeline and a validated lower-memory generator checkpoint.
operator_setup: Register document collections, permitted pinned model profiles, acceptance tests, access keys and the operator W&B project. The Sera worker and caller run on the same host.

workload.acceptance_source: Operator-supplied synthetic regression tests. These were earlier failed independent tests and are no longer held out.

result.board: Astra assigns 15 roles; 15 Luna specialists propose and rank recipes; Astra reviews repeated results. All 32 board calls use Codex ChatGPT login.
result.memory_metric_scope: MLX allocator; not system-wide unified memory or free VRAM
result.latency_scope: Generator-only latency on frozen retrieved contexts; two measurement blocks, not a statistical speedup claim.

limits: The 100,000 documents are short synthetic records, not customer documents or enterprise RAG certification.
Generator quantization is optimized on frozen retrieved contexts. Retrieval settings are selected at intake, not jointly searched.
Generated questions missed real regressions in earlier attempts; supplied acceptance tests remain necessary for customer quality requirements.
A previous run of the final code exhausted the five-minute confirmation budget and returned baseline. Savings are not guaranteed within every five-minute run.
Memory measures the MLX allocator, not system-wide unified memory or free NVIDIA VRAM.
Extractive citation checks establish phrase support, not full semantic correctness.
The new prompt-to-RAG flow has been run on MLX. Existing CUDA optimization has separate evidence; this RAG flow has no live CUDA or ROCm validation.
The client uses a loopback service and server-local model/index paths. This release is not a remote multi-tenant SaaS.
No fixed-search superiority, global optimality or world-first claim is established.
